newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico gives partial final results from election.
newsitem.headline: Mexico gives partial final results from election.

text.p: Mexico's Federal Electoral Institute (IFE) gave partial final results from Sunday's mid-term elections late on Wednesday. A completed tally was not expected until late on Thursday.

Results from 84 of 300 directly-elected districts showed the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) winning 44 races, following by the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) with 22.
The conservative National Action Party (PAN) had won 18 seats, the results showed.
A complete count of the congressional races would be available late on Thursday, Felipe Solis Acero, technical secretary of the IFE, told Reuters.
In addition to the 300 seats, some 200 others will be assigned according to each party's share of the overall vote.

IFE gave results Monday night from a preliminary count of 86 percent of polling stations, showing the ruling PRI likely to lose its majority in the lower house of Congress with a 38.8 percent share of the national vote.
The results, however, did not include some rural areas where the PRI has traditionally enjoyed strong support.

Mexico City's Reforma newspaper estimated on Wednesday that if the trend in the first 86 percent of preliminary results held, the PRI would end up 13 seats short of a majority in the 500-seat Chamber of Deputies.
The PRI also lost the Mexico City mayoral race to a left-wing opposition leader in the worst trouncing in its seven decades in power.
The IFE's governing General Council adjourned on Monday evening after giving the preliminary numbers and resumed work on Wednesday.
Solis Acero said the 300 electoral districts across the country would work non-stop to tally the final figures for the congressional races.
